services.title: Eight deliverables. One legal team.
services.description: Everything required to move from "we want to sell in Mexico" to a fully compliant, marketplace-approved operation — in the order you'll actually need it.

items.label: Entity
items.title: Mexican Company Formation for Foreign Owners
items.description: Structuring and incorporating your Mexican entity (SA or SAS de CV) with the correct foreign-ownership structure, shareholder / legal representative setup, and minimum capital compliance.

items.label: Tax ID
items.title: RFC (Mexican Tax ID) Registration
items.description: Obtaining your company's RFC with SAT — the tax registration required before you can invoice, open a business bank account, or register on any marketplace.

items.label: Address
items.title: Legal Business Address (Domicilio Fiscal)
items.description: Establishing a compliant registered business address in Mexico, required for SAT registration and marketplace verification.

items.label: Brand
items.title: Trademark Classification & Registration (IMPI)
items.description: Filing your brand under the correct trademark classification with Mexico's Industrial Property Institute — protecting your name before launch, and satisfying marketplace brand-registry requirements where applicable.

items.label: Permits
items.title: Industry-Specific Government Permits
items.description: Identifying and obtaining the permits required for your specific product category or service line — cosmetics, electronics, food-adjacent products, and others each carry different regulatory requirements in Mexico.

items.label: Certified
items.title: Fully Certified, Verification-Ready Documentation
items.description: Every document issued carries the correct official government stamps, signatures, holograms, electronic certification, and QR verification codes — built to pass scrutiny from SAT, a bank, or a marketplace's review team.

items.label: Platform
items.title: Marketplace Approval Documentation
items.description: Preparing your legal and tax documentation specifically for category approval and seller verification on Amazon Mexico, Mercado Libre, and TikTok Shop — formatted the way each platform's compliance review actually expects to see it.

items.label: Operate
items.title: Import, Sales & Production Legal Guidance
items.description: Ongoing legal guidance for importing and selling physical products in Mexico, or for establishing a production or assembly facility — including IMMEX program eligibility and shelter-provider arrangements where relevant.

faq.title: Straight answers before you book a call.

items.title: How long does it take to legally start selling on Amazon Mexico, Mercado Libre, or TikTok Shop?
items.content: Incorporation and RFC typically take 2–4 weeks. Running compliance work in parallel, most clients are ready to submit marketplace documentation within 4–6 weeks of starting — timelines depend on your product category and any permits it requires.

items.title: Do I need a Mexican citizen as a shareholder or legal representative?
items.content: Not necessarily a shareholder, but foreign-owned entities do need a Mexican legal representative for certain filings. We'll walk you through the structure that fits your ownership and risk preferences, including what documentation we require before taking on that role.

items.title: What is the RFC and why do I need it before I can operate?
items.content: The RFC is your company's tax ID with SAT, Mexico's tax authority. You need it to invoice, open a business bank account, and register as a seller on any Mexican marketplace — it's the foundation everything else is built on.

items.title: Can I qualify for IMMEX or a shelter-provider program if I plan to manufacture or assemble in Mexico?
items.content: Depends on your product, import volume, and operating model. We review eligibility as part of the diagnosis stage and explain what a shelter-provider arrangement would look like in practice for your specific case.

items.title: What documentation will Amazon, Mercado Libre, or TikTok actually require to approve my account?
items.content: Typically your incorporation documents, RFC, proof of business address, and — for certain categories — specific permits or certifications. We prepare the package in the format each platform's review team expects.

items.title: Is a Mexican entity required for each product category or storefront, or can one entity operate multiple stores?
items.content: One entity can generally operate multiple storefronts. We'll advise on the structure that makes sense for your situation rather than defaulting to unnecessary complexity.

items.title: What ongoing compliance is required after incorporation?
items.content: Monthly accounting and SAT filings, IMSS reporting if you have employees, and annual filings. We outline this clearly before you commit, so there are no surprises after day one.

items.title: What language is used for documentation and consultations?
items.content: Contracts, filings, and this page are available in Chinese and English. Live consultations are conducted in English; interpretation support can be arranged on request so your team has full clarity at every stage.
